narrator.rule: The narrator only says what the profile says. Every sentence can be traced to a section, a claim or the music/movement DNA.
narrator.identity: one narrator for the whole atlas: the same face and animation everywhere; a native-speaker voice of the same character per language (studio-grade); the viewer chooses the language

scenes.title: Where and when
narration: The Branyo developed from the corridinho, a traditional folk dance from the Algarve region of Portugal, brought to Malaysia by early Portuguese colonists who arrived in Malacca in the 16th century.
It has been preserved for centuries by their modern-day descendants, the Malaccan Portuguese community.

Over time, the dance became deeply embedded in the local cultural landscape, where it eventually influenced and enriched Malay performance traditions, giving rise to the popular Malay dance known as the Joget.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: The Branyo is an integral part of Introdu, the traditional Malaccan Portuguese festival celebrated on Shrove Sunday (Quinquagesima), immediately preceding Ash Wednesday and the season of Lent.
It serves as a vital expression of Malaccan Portuguese heritage and communal identity.
Today it is a living tradition.
